precepts.text: The men knew that their wives burned incense unto other gods, and the people told Jeremiah plainly, we will not hearken unto thee; the same spirit is on brothers today who know their wives are in the midst of evil and will not check them.
precepts.point: Then the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the Lord only. That is repentance.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

precepts.why:
“Then all the men which knew that their wives had burned incense unto other gods, and all the women that stood by, a great multitude” answered Jeremiah: “As for the word that thou hast spoken unto us in the name of the Lord, we will not hearken unto thee.”

The men knew what their wives were doing, and they stood with it. The same spirit is on brothers today who know their wives are in the midst of evil and will not check them.

This is the same worship Samuel told Israel to put away. Who is Ashtoreth? Astaroth in demonology is a chief figure of hell, named after the Near Eastern goddess Astarte, and Astarte is the Hellenized form of Ashtoreth, a form of Ishtar, the goddess called the queen of heaven, associated with love, beauty, sex, and war. Samuel was exhorting the people to depart from these fake gods and goddesses of the nations, and to this day there are Israelites that have not put away Ashtoreth from among them.

precepts.text: We will burn incense unto the queen of heaven, for then had we plenty of victuals; since we left off, we have wanted all things. That is Ishtar worship, and it is the same spirit that says, when I was in the world celebrating her holidays I was good, and now in the truth I am catching hell.
precepts.point: Then the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the Lord only. That is repentance.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

precepts.why:
The people told Jeremiah plainly: “we will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth forth out of our own mouth, to burn incense unto the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her.” And their reason: “for then had we plenty of victuals, and were well, and saw no evil. But since we left off to burn incense to the queen of heaven … we have wanted all things, and have been consumed by the sword and by the famine.”

That is Ishtar worship, the queen of heaven, the same Ashtaroth Samuel told Israel to put away. And it is the same spirit that says, when I was in the world celebrating her holidays I was good, and now in the truth I am catching hell.

Easter is at its roots the celebration of Ishtar, the goddess of fertility and sex. When Constantine set out to merge paganism with the faith of the apostles to bring everything under one empire, pagan rituals like Easter and Saturnalia were dressed up as honoring Christ, and that was the birth of Roman Catholicism. Nothing about it mathematically adds up to Christ rising, the apostles never celebrated it or taught it, and a bunny laying eggs has nothing to do with your Lord and Saviour; it is not of Christ.

So put her away, as Israel did: “Then the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the Lord only.”

precepts.text: The prophets come out of the nation of Israel and no other, because the Most High is in the midst of Israel and none else and the Bible is given to the Israelites and none else.
precepts.point: The same work goes on today; we fill up the street corners all over the earth bringing forth the glorious gospel of the one true living God and Christ, the prophets He raised up to give warning.

note.label: Jeremiah 44: The Judgment on the Jews Who Fled to Egypt

precepts.why:
The Lord sent “all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them”, pleading with the Jews in Egypt not to do the abominable thing he hates. Amos shows where those prophets come from: “And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.”

The prophets come out of the nation of Israel and no other, because the Most High is in the midst of Israel and none else, and the Bible is given to the Israelites and none else. The same work goes on today: we fill up the street corners all over the earth bringing forth the glorious gospel of the one true living God and Christ, the prophets he raised up of our own sons to give warning.

precepts.text: He that sins against the Most High wrongs his own soul, for the wages of sin is death, and they that hate Him love death.
precepts.point: They provoke Him to wrath with the works of their hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where they had gone to dwell, cutting themselves off to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth.

note.label: Jeremiah 44: The Judgment on the Jews Who Fled to Egypt

precepts.why:
The Lord asks the Jews in Egypt, “Wherefore commit ye this great evil against your souls”, cutting off man and woman, child and suckling out of Judah. Solomon says how sin does that: “But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: all they that hate me love death.”

He that sins against the Most High wrongs his own soul, for the wages of sin is death. Burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt was not only provoking him to wrath with the works of their hands; it was cutting themselves off to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations. They that hate him love death, and that is the great evil they committed against their own souls.

precepts.text: All these curses of the law shall come upon them, pursue them, and overtake them until they are destroyed, even those who sought refuge in Egypt, because they hearkened not to the voice of the Most High.
precepts.point: They shall become an execration, an astonishment, a curse, and a reproach; only a small number escaping the sword shall return, for none shall return to Judah though they have a desire to dwell there.

note.label: Jeremiah 44: The Judgment on the Jews Who Fled to Egypt

precepts.why:
The remnant of Judah that set their faces to go into Egypt would be consumed by the sword and the famine, from the least to the greatest, and become an execration, an astonishment, a curse and a reproach. Moses had written that the curses follow: “Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed; because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded thee”.

All these curses of the law come upon them, pursue them, and overtake them until they are destroyed, even those who sought refuge in Egypt. They were not humbled even to that day, nor did they fear or walk in his law and his statutes, so fleeing Jerusalem did not escape the curse; it pursued them into Egypt, and none returned to Judah but such as escaped.

precepts.text: The Most High declares there is no god with Him; He kills and makes alive, wounds and heals, and none can deliver out of His hand, so when He swears a counsel by His own name it stands.
precepts.point: Evil does not come merely by chance; the Most High brings that evil upon us when we turn from Him and follow our own mind, sinning against the one true living God in Christ.

note.label: Jeremiah 44: The Judgment on the Jews Who Fled to Egypt

precepts.why:
The Lord gives a sign that his words shall surely stand against them for evil: Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt will be given into the hand of his enemies, as Zedekiah was given into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar. He can promise that because “See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.”

There is no god with him. He kills and makes alive, wounds and heals, and none can deliver out of his hand, not Pharaoh's gods and not Egypt's army. So when he swears a counsel by his own name it stands, and the Jews that fled to Egypt for safety would see the king they trusted in fall as their own king fell.

precepts.text: If a trumpet is blown in the city the people are afraid, and there is no evil in the city that the Most High has not done, so we cannot attribute everything bad to the devil.
precepts.point: Evil does not come merely by chance; the Most High brings that evil upon us when we turn from Him and follow our own mind, sinning against the one true living God in Christ.

note.label: Jeremiah 44: The Judgment on the Jews Who Fled to Egypt

precepts.why:
“I will punish you in this place, that ye may know that my words shall surely stand against you for evil”. Evil does not come merely by chance. Amos asks: “Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid? shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it?”

If a trumpet is blown in the city the people are afraid, and there is no evil in the city that the Most High has not done. So we cannot attribute everything bad to the devil. The Most High brings that evil upon us when we turn from him and follow our own mind, sinning against the one true living God in Christ, just as he brought it on Zedekiah and would bring it on Pharaoh-hophra and the Jews in Egypt.
